los.text: Identify organelles and structures within the cell membranes and link them to function and likely pathology
los.html:
StructureFunctionPathology
NucleusDNA, transcription; nucleolus makes rRNAMutations, cancer; pyknosis and karyorrhexis in cell death
Rough ERProteins for secretion and membranesProminent in plasma cells; Nissl bodies in neurons
Smooth ERLipid and steroid synthesis, drug detoxification, Ca²⁺ store (sarcoplasmic reticulum)Enzyme induction (e.g. by alcohol, rifampicin)
GolgiModifies, sorts and packages proteins; adds mannose-6-phosphate to lysosomal enzymesI-cell disease (enzymes secreted instead of reaching lysosomes)
LysosomesAcid hydrolases digest materialLysosomal storage diseases (Tay–Sachs, Gaucher)
MitochondriaATP (oxidative phosphorylation); release cytochrome c in apoptosisMaternally inherited mitochondrial disease (MELAS); ragged red fibres
PeroxisomesVery-long-chain fatty acid oxidation, catalaseZellweger syndrome, adrenoleukodystrophy
RibosomesProtein synthesis: human 80SBacterial 70S ribosomes are targets for aminoglycosides, macrolides, tetracyclines
MicrotubulesMitotic spindle, cilia, axonal transportDrug targets: colchicine, vincristine, taxanes; primary ciliary dyskinesia (Kartagener)
Intermediate filamentsStrength (keratin, vimentin, desmin, GFAP, neurofilaments)Used as tumour markers to show cell origin
Actin microfilamentsCell shape, movement, microvilliListeria uses host actin to spread between cells
Structure in the membraneFunctionPathology
Phospholipid bilayer + cholesterolSelective barrier, fluiditySpherocytosis (membrane skeleton)
Channels and transportersMove ions and moleculesCFTR chloride channel in cystic fibrosis
ReceptorsHormone and drug bindingGraves' (TSH receptor antibodies), myasthenia (ACh receptor)
Tight junctionsSeal between cells (barrier)Bacterial toxins open them (e.g. C. difficile)
DesmosomesAnchor cells to each otherPemphigus vulgaris (antibodies to desmoglein)
HemidesmosomesAnchor cells to the basement membraneBullous pemphigoid
Gap junctionsConnexin channels between cellsSpread of cardiac and smooth muscle excitation
GlycocalyxRecognition, adhesionPathogens bind its sugars to enter cells
Bacteria vs human cells
  • No nucleus, 70S ribosomes, peptidoglycan cell wall (penicillins), different membrane sterols (fungi: ergosterol, target of azoles).
  • These differences allow selective toxicity.
Intracellular infectionViruses hijack ribosomes and ER; TB survives by blocking phagosome–lysosome fusion; Chlamydia and Rickettsia are obligate intracellular.
